description: Spread over 30 acres in Sector 16, Asia's largest rose garden established in 1967 named after India's third President, showcasing over 50,000 rose bushes across 1,600 unique species alongside medicinal tree groves.
why_visit: Wander through vast fragrant beds of blossoming roses, attend the spectacular annual Rose Festival in February, and relax by illuminated fountains.
best_time_to_visit: October to March (6:00 AM - 8:00 PM; peak bloom February/March)
activities: Rose Photography; Botanical Walking; Annual Rose Festival Attendance; Picnics
notes: Features the annual 3-day Rose Festival with cultural performances and flower shows.

description: Designed by master architect Le Corbusier and opened in 1968, housing a world-class collection of 2nd-century Gandharan Buddhist stone sculptures, Pahari and Rajasthani miniature paintings, and contemporary Indian art.
why_visit: Admire pure Le Corbusier modernist architecture, stand before exquisite ancient Gandhara Buddha sculptures, and inspect rare lyrical Pahari miniature paintings.
activities: Gandhara Art Appreciation; Le Corbusier Architecture Tour; Miniature Painting Study
notes: A portion of the Gandhara collection originated from the Central Museum in Lahore.

subcategory: Le Corbusier's 8-Km Continuous Linear Green Belt
description: An 8-kilometer continuous emerald green belt envisioned by Le Corbusier as the 'Lungs of Chandigarh', connecting 12 themed parks (Bougainvillea, Rose Garden, Shanti Kunj) along a seasonal eroded valley.
why_visit: Cycle or walk along an uninterrupted 8-km green corridor running through the entire heart of the city without crossing busy traffic intersections.
activities: Linear Park Cycling; Jogging; Photography; Open-Air Cultural Concerts
notes: Hosts the annual Chandigarh Carnival with cultural floats and art installations.

description: A 20-acre landscaped park in Sector 3 showcasing over 65 vibrant varieties of bougainvillea trained over arches, pavilions, and bowers, housing the National War Memorial honoring martyrs of the armed forces.
why_visit: Admire vibrant cascades of purple, magenta, and white bougainvillea blooms, pay homage at the War Memorial, and walk under fitness fitness trails.
activities: Bougainvillea Photography; War Memorial Homage; Morning Fitness Walk
notes: The National War Memorial on site was inaugurated in 2006 by President APJ Abdul Kalam.

subcategory: Nek Chand's World-Renowned 40-Acre Recycled Sculpture Fantasy
description: Secretly created by government road inspector Nek Chand starting in 1957, a surreal 40-acre visionary kingdom of winding courtyards, gorges, waterfalls, and thousands of sculptures made entirely from industrial, ceramic, and domestic urban waste.
why_visit: Step through tiny stone doorways into a fantasy world of dancing sculptures made from broken bangles, discarded tiles, ceramic electrical sockets, and sit beneath rushing waterfalls.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round (9:00 AM - 7:00 PM summer, until 6:00 PM winter)
activities: Recycled Art Exploration; Courtyard Photography; Waterfall Viewing; Sculpture Appreciation
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: Sector 1, between Capitol Complex and Sukhna Lake
notes: Welcomes over 5,000 visitors daily; recognized globally as a masterpiece of outsider art.

description: Designed by master architect Le Corbusier as part of the UNESCO World Heritage Capitol Complex, an open-sided concrete brise-soleil pavilion constructed so that no ray of sunlight penetrates its interior throughout the year.
why_visit: Marvel at Le Corbusier's genius in solar geometry and tropical brise-soleil shading, and tour the Open Hand Monument and High Court inside the UNESCO complex.
best_time_to_visit: Year-round (Guided tours 10:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 3:00 PM via Tourist Center)
activities: UNESCO Modernist Architecture Tour; Solar Geometry Study; Photography
notes: Inscribed as an UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016 as part of Le Corbusier's works.
